page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores, 15 GB of system memory, and a dedicated NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data. The CPU supports AVX and AVX-512 extensions, alongside AES cryptographic hardware instructions.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinct contrast between CPU capabilities and hardware accelerator throughput. General-purpose CPU scores sit in lower percentiles, as demonstrated by Geekbench results (933 single-core and 2077 multi-core) and PassMark CPU metrics (3647.3). Memory bandwidth testing shows 20.81 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks, aligning with lower benchmark bands. Conversely, GPU-accelerated inference tasks perform robustly. Prompt processing for a 7B parameter LLM achieves 1167.65 tokens per second, scoring in the top 10 percent, while text generation produces 34.5 tokens per second, ranking in the top 25 percent.

From an efficiency standpoint, the ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge delivers cost-effective acceleration for workloads designed specifically to offload computational complexity to the GPU. Because raw CPU and host memory bandwidth are constrained, this configuration offers high economic utility when serving machine learning inference, real-time video transcoding, or lightweight graphics pipelines, but serves poorly as a host for compute-heavy compilation or purely CPU-bound database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores) on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor, 15 GB of RAM, and a single NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Operating over KVM with a 4 Gbps baseline network and no bundled local storage, its architecture prioritizes accelerated workloads. In benchmark tests, general CPU performance and host memory bandwidth rank in lower tiers, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2077. In contrast, the NVIDIA T4 yields top-tier LLM inference performance, reaching 1167.65 tokens per second on prompt processing for 7B models. This makes the instance an efficient fit for machine learning inference, model evaluation, and GPU-driven media processing rather than CPU-bound tasks.
